overreach: RFIC validation increasingly needs realistic stimulus: modulated waveforms, multi-carrier cases, coexistence/interference, beam/OTA conditions, and corner-case stress tests.
Signal generators therefore need wider modulation bandwidth, better waveform fidelity, multi-carrier generation, phase-coherent channels, and automation-friendly waveform control.
RFICs are validated not only by conducted RF tests but also in system-like environments: chambers, OTA, software-controlled setups, and linked generator/analyzer workflows.
Modern RFIC validation benefits from tightly synchronized generation and capture: EVM, ACLR, spurious, compression, memory effects, group delay, phase noise, and transient behavior...
Higher frequency coverage for mmWave and future bands.
Higher dynamic range for ACPR/ACLR, blocker, intermodulation, and spurious testing.
Multi-channel phase coherence for MIMO, beamforming, phased-array, and differential RFIC tests.
as RFIC validation moves from component-level, manually configured tests toward automated, realistic, system-level validation...
